issue: जेवर सुत हरि भक्त निकन्दन — निकन्दन ('destroyer') has no object; read as two epithets, a devotee of Hari and a destroyer (of the wicked). It could be 'destroyer of (the troubles of) Hari's devotees'.
our reading: he is a devotee of Hari and a destroyer (of the wicked).
alternatives: destroyer of the sorrows of Hari's devotees.

issue: आप बने सुर भूप — read plainly as 'a king among the gods' (deified); it could mean 'a god-like king' or 'king of heroes' (सूर).
our reading: you became a king among the gods.
alternatives: you became a divine king; you became king of heroes (सूर).

issue: चरण पकड़कर पिण्ड छुड़ाया । सिंह भवन माड़ी बनवाया — the subject is not named: Anaṅgpāl (who laid down his arms in chaupāī 47) clasped Gūgā's feet to free himself; who had the shrine built is left open (Anaṅgpāl, or Gūgā for his own samādhi). सिंह भवन read as 'a lion's abode' (Gūgā, the lion of do1); it may be a place name. माड़ी read as मढ़ी (shrine), as in the Jāharvīr Āratī.
our reading: Clasping his feet, he got himself free; a lion's abode, a shrine, was built.
alternatives: Anaṅgpāl had a shrine built at Siṃha Bhavan; Gūgā had a māṛī built, a lion's dwelling.

issue: गोरख टीला धूनी रमाये — the subject read as Gūgā (as in the first half, समाये); it could be Gorakh lighting his dhūnī at the Ṭīlā.
our reading: he kindled the ascetic's fire on Gorakh Ṭīlā.
alternatives: Gorakh kindled his dhūnī on the Ṭīlā.
